slides.text: PEOPLE STILL MARK HER TOMB TO MAKE A WISH
New Orleans. St. Louis Cemetery No. 1, founded in 1789: the oldest cemetery still standing in the city.
The dead here rest above ground, in tombs of brick and plaster.
One tomb is believed to hold Marie Laveau, the city's famous voodoo priestess. She died in 1881.
The legend: draw three X's on her tomb, make a wish... and she'll grant it.
Thousands did. Marker. Lipstick. Scratches in the stone.
People left coins, flowers and gifts in the cracks.
Then someone painted her whole tomb pink.
Since 2015, you can only go inside with a registered tour guide.
